pages.transcription:
The Wyndham Hotel 42 West 58 Street	5. April 1941
Dear Hannah & Manfred, I wrote you these days about my taxes
with which I have to worry you as you have the statements, I hope
you have {and will communicate} already my letter. Today what will please you more
- that we shall have Eva here for her holidays one week and I hope
she will enjoy New York more than she did before. We will talk a lot
about you.
Lotte has behaved badly against me, as I wrote you, and is now be-
having costly. As her attacks of asthma did not stop we were obliged
to let examine her thoroughly for I want for my work and travelling
a wife and secretary who keeps fit. Dr. Schür, whom I know from
London, (he has been the doctor of Sigmund Freud) has seen her
and now with a specialist he is making tests to find out the allergic
points. It is not a serious state as you know, but before we go
away I would like to have her examined as well as possible; I doubt
if we could find on another place such competent persons. Do not
think therefore that it is serious; I want only to prevent a setback
when we would have to travel again. Our plans are not at all fixed
up - who can decide in a time like ours? - but we will stay in any
case till to the end of May here in New York.
We have read here in the newspapers about attacks on Bristol and
I hope you have been had no visit of this kind in Bath, which is
so near. I hope also that 17 Orchard has no damage and that all
is going quietly as before. Here the preparations seem to be enor-
mous and we hope all that they will become sufficient et effective
in a short time.
Perhaps I shall have to speak here at a dinner at the Pen Club
(only a few minutes) on April 29th at the opening of the Euro-
pean Branch; if so it will be relayed by short wave and you could
perhaps hear me. I hate dinner speaks but I do not know if it will
be possible to escape. Kindest regards to you all yours Stefan Zweig
